questions.question: Describe one feature of each of the four rocky planets.
questions.expected_answer: Mercury is the smallest planet and closest to the Sun, with almost no air, many craters and no moons. Venus is almost the size of Earth, has thick clouds that trap heat so it is the hottest planet, and has no moons. Earth is the only planet known to have liquid water, breathable air and life, and it has one moon. Mars is the red planet, because of rusted iron in its dust, and it has two small moons.

questions.question: Describe one feature of each of the four gas giants.
questions.expected_answer: Jupiter is the biggest planet, with a giant storm called the Great Red Spot and more than ninety moons. Saturn has bright, wide rings of ice and rock and the most moons of any planet. Uranus is tipped on its side and rolls around the Sun. Neptune is the furthest planet from the Sun, deep blue, with the strongest winds in the Solar System.

questions.question: Explain how a planet's position affects its year, and why Venus breaks the temperature pattern.
questions.expected_answer: The further a planet is from the Sun, the longer its orbit and the more slowly it moves, so its year is longer: Mercury takes eighty-eight days, Earth three hundred and sixty-five days and Neptune about one hundred and sixty-five Earth years. Most planets get colder further from the Sun, but Venus is hotter than Mercury because its thick clouds trap the Sun's heat.
